title: The folder called final
label: THE FOLDER CALLED FINAL
lead: Hook 1, because almost everyone has a 'final' file that isn't, and frame 0 can show that folder name on the screen.

hooks.label: THE FOLDER CALLED FINAL
hooks.say: There's a folder on your laptop called *final*, and it's nowhere near final.

hooks.label: SAVED FOREVER. NEVER OPENED.
hooks.say: Your laptop keeps every half-finished idea safe, and you never open them.

hooks.label: WHERE YOUR BEST IDEAS GO
hooks.say: Why does the idea you loved most end up buried in a folder?

beats.say: There's a folder on your laptop called *final*, and it's nowhere near final.
beats.scene: A dark desk. A laptop flips open fast; on the screen, one amber folder named FINAL. A cursor hovers, and the folder shudders on 'nowhere'.

beats.say: Inside is a plan you were so sure about, and a *draft* that stops mid-sentence.
beats.scene: Close and angled on the screen. A tidy plan page, then on 'draft' a page whose last line stops halfway, the caret blinking.

beats.say: Every time you see it, you *close* the laptop, because finishing feels huge.
beats.scene: Wide side view, one desk lamp. On 'close' the lid shuts, the screen glow dies and the room drops into lamplight.

beats.say: So open it tonight and do one *small* part, like fixing a single page.
beats.scene: Straight down from above. The lid lifts on 'open'; on 'small' one line on the page turns amber and a progress bar ticks forward a sliver.

beats.say: Then rename that folder something honest, like *started again*.
beats.scene: Morning light, warm sand room. Flat-on screen: the name FINAL is deleted letter by letter and 'started again' types in.

beats.say: Send this to the friend with a folder called final, final, *really final*.
beats.scene: The screen fills with folders: final, final_2, final_FINAL, really_final, multiplying as the camera pulls back from the laptop.
